what_happened: The job was meant to move the Early pull request and CI wait row from gh/mod.rs into gh/early.rs. It was rejected at the final verdict. One of 7 acceptance criteria was unmet: no lower-row module (transport, remote, client, pages, records) may name early, and early.rs may use only host, client and transport siblings, with no circular use. One major finding: the move creates a client <-> early dependency cycle (client.rs:5 and :74 refer to early; early.rs:7-10 uses client). The design document says such a cycle must stop the job. No failed checks are listed. The other 6 criteria were met, so the move itself may be otherwise sound.
cause: Nothing in code checks the layering rule of the gh module split. The rule says lower rows must not name higher rows and there must be no cycles. It lives only in the design document and in a criterion, and is judged only when the verifier reads the diff at the final verdict, where rejection is the only outcome. The producer and the checks never look at the dependency direction between rows. Neither the plan nor the reading says where client's use of early must go, such as moving the shared item to a lower row. So the cycle appears only after the code is moved. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the producer's work.
prevention: Add a repo test or xtask check that reads the gh module's use and path references and fails on any reference from a lower row (transport, remote, client, pages, records) to a higher row, and on any cycle among rows. The check should run with the job's other checks so the producer sees the violation before handover. The check would stop this whole class: structural rules from the design document being found only at the final verdict.
proposed_request: Move the Early pull request and CI wait row from gh/mod.rs to a new gh/early.rs, following the row order in the gh design document. Outcome: no lower-row module (transport, remote, client, pages, records) names early, early.rs uses only host, client and transport siblings, and there is no circular use. client.rs currently refers to early (around lines 5 and 74), so first work out what client needs from it and move that item to a lower row, or change the call so the dependency points one way. Add a test that fails on any upward reference or cycle among the gh rows. Behavior must not change: existing tests and the usual checks pass. Report each moved name and the result of the dependency-direction test.
